title: Establish GPU compatibility profiles and CI environment capture for regression-proof load tests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Load harness results (tokens/sec, p95 latency) are not reliably reproducible across CI runs because the underlying GPU runtime environment drifts: driver/CUDA combinations, kernel modules, image digest changes, and runner configuration vary between runners. We need a reproducible, auditable approach to capture and freeze the exact runtime environment used for each benchmark run and to formalize a compatibility matrix of supported GPU stacks so regression detection is meaningful and actionable.

Goal: Define GPU compatibility profiles (driver + CUDA + cuDNN + kernel) and a CI capture pipeline that produces an immutable environment artifact for every load test run. Integrate environment artifacts with the benchmarking harness and the regression detector so operators can trace performance regressions to environment drift, model changes, or runtime bugs.

Scope:
- Define a minimal supported matrix of driver / CUDA / cuDNN combinations for the runners we use in load harnesses (A100/MI250/RTX6000 families).
- Add an "env-capture" step to the benchmark runner that records driver version, CUDA toolkit version, cuDNN, kernel uname, NVML output, container image digest, libcuda ABI checksums, and GPU firmware identifiers.
- Standardize runner image tags and include digest capture in artifacts.
- Wire environment artifacts into CI storage (S3) and include an index accessible from the benchmark dashboard.
- Nightly smoke job: run baseline scenarios, store tokens/sec and p95 metrics alongside environment artifact.
- Implement a regression detection rule set that compares current metrics to baseline for the same compatibility profile and triggers alerts when regressions exceed thresholds.

Out of scope for this ticket: actual fixes to drivers or kernels; broadening the matrix beyond initial families listed above.
acceptance_criteria: A compatibility matrix doc exists listing at least 3 tested driver+CUDA profiles (one per GPU family) and owners for each profile
env-capture script runs inside benchmark runners and produces a JSON environment artifact containing driver, CUDA, cuDNN, kernel, NVML output, container image digest, and timestamps
CI pipeline stores environment artifacts and metrics to S3 with a stable index URL and links visible from the benchmark dashboard

Nightly baseline job executes 3 standard load scenarios and records tokens/sec and p95; regression detector runs and raises a ticket and Slack alert if >5% drop in throughput or >10% increase in p95 for the same profile
Documentation + runbook on triaging environment-related regressions published in Confluence and linked from the dashboard

comments: 2026-02-18 Aisha Patel: Created ticket. Initial spike completed: enumerated 9 runner images across CI and prod. Observed 4 distinct driver/CUDA combos in use. Attached short doc with raw outputs.

2026-02-23 Marco Liu: Architecture review - proposed tagging scheme 'profile:<gpu_family>-cuda<xx>-drv<yyy>-digest' to make profiles human readable and machine parsable. Shared draft RFC: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INF/Env+Capture+RFC

2026-02-27 Ethan Ross: Implemented a first pass of env-capture (bash + nvmlinfo) and pushed to branch env-capture-cli. Small binary emits JSON with keys driver_version, cuda_version, cudnn_version, kernel, container_digest, nvml_raw. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/492
2026-03-03 Nina Gomez (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria, requested that nightly baseline include p95 and p99 tails and store raw token traces for a minimum 10-minute run window for each scenario.

2026-03-08 QA: Ran env-capture in the staging runner pool (A100 x4) and uploaded sample artifact: s3://redwood-benchmarks/env-artifacts/staging/2026-03-08-a100-profile.json. Baseline run metrics: tokens/sec=1760, p95=32ms, p99=75ms. Will compare next run for drift.

2026-03-12 Priya Menon: Regression detector prototype deployed to our test cluster. Detector compares current run to the 7-day moving baseline for the same profile. Thresholds: throughput drop >5% or p95 increase >10% triggers alert. Prototype found one false-positive; adjusted smoothing window to 3 days for low-signal profiles.

2026-03-14 Marco Liu: Added CI validator that fails PRs when the env-capture output contains an unsupported driver+CUDA pair. Validator uses the compatibility matrix file in /bench-config/compatibility-profiles.yaml. Opening follow-ups to expand the matrix and add architecture-level approval for exceptions.
